Shifting Demand Landscape
• Pressurized consumer budgets over the period triggered slower
volume growth and increased downtrading activities. Widespread
price pressures in the real economy led to reprioritized spending, as real
income growth trailed behind inflation rates. This led to consumer
affordability challenges, especially in the Kenyan market. This invariably
correlated with higher illicit consumption incidences over the period.
• Demand remained relatively resilient in offshore markets,
especially in fast-growing markets such as DRC. However, regulatory
changes in key offshore markets, as well as geopolitical tensions in the Horn
of Africa region piled pressure on revenue performance.
• Management also anticipates fast growth in emerging business
lines notably non-combustibles. The product which has been the subject
of regulatory tiffs, compelled the firm to halt its marketing, despite having
launched a non-combustibles factory. However, the manufacturer signaled at
finalization of compliance with regulatory requirements and are ready to
accelerate marketing efforts.
The Terrain Ahead
• The firm’s acceleration of the cost to income ratio led to a notable decline
in the return on equity below pre-pandemic levels. However, we note the
strong efficiency in conversion of operating profits into free cash flows.
• Strong free cashflow conversion, low leverage as well as minimal capital
spending needs over the medium-term horizon supported an increase in the
firm’s dividend payout ratio.
• Management has adjusted to the mounting volatility on the Kenya shilling
over recent months, by maintaining sufficient dollar-denominated working
capital to hedge against such excessive exchange rate risks.

Recommendation
• We maintain our HOLD recommendation on BAT Kenya, on account of its sharp declining return on equity, yet
remain cautiously optimistic for a robust recovery in consumer demand and sustained cost efficiencies over the
medium-term. We expect the firm’s bottom-line to remain sensitive to exchange rate volatility and input price shocks over the
year. Our one-year target price for BAT Kenya currently stands at KES 460.75 - representing a c.11.4% upside potential from current
levels.
